title: Reimagine Quickstart landing: compact hero, interactive system-diagram, progressive step cards
creator: Leah Kim
description:
Scope: Create a compact, scannable Quickstart landing experience that supports three asset families: 1) a compact hero variant optimized for developer scan patterns and small viewports; 2) an interactive system-diagram that visualizes request routing across Hosted / Dedicated / Private with fallback flows; 3) progressive step cards (3-5 steps) with annotated product screenshots and copy hooks for docs and marketing reuse.

Goals:
- Improve convertibility of Quickstart by surfacing the 3-minute onboarding path and concrete sample code quickly.
- Provide a single set of production-ready assets (Figma + exported PNG/SVG + annotated screenshots) that can be used in docs, marketing, and release notes.
- Ensure accessibility: high-contrast variants, motion-reduced exports, and screen-reader friendly step semantics.

Deliverables:
- Compact hero: primary + alt layout for narrow hero bars, CTA variants (Primary/Secondary/Inline link), micro-illustration set (3 assets). Export specs: 2x PNG, SVG, WebP.
- Interactive system-diagram: three-layer diagram (client -> smart-router -> model pools) with hover states that reveal latency/cost tradeoffs. Deliver two modes: static SVG for docs and a lightweight JS-enabled prototype for Console.
- Progressive step cards: 3 canonical cards (Connect, Run, Optimize) with screenshot overlays showing SDK snippet, Console route, and cost/latency tooltip. Export PNGs at 1200x800 and responsive slices for mobile.
- Asset inventory and naming convention, accessibility checklist, and a short handoff doc for engineering/marketing.

Acceptance criteria:
- All assets are exported and uploaded to the shared Figma library and artifacts folder with tokenized names.
- Hero and step cards pass WCAG AA contrast; motion-reduced variants exist and are flagged.
- Interactive diagram prototype tested in Console staging by ENG-5182 and matches routing behavior in the runtime docs.
- PM sign-off on copy and conversion messaging; UX research quick A/B plan prepared for post-launch.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Chose compact hero to reduce vertical fold on marketing pages; this trades some illustrative storytelling for quicker code visibility.
- Interactive diagram uses progressively enhanced SVG with a small JS shim to avoid heavy frameworks in docs.
- Screenshots will use real Console routes but masked with example tokens and obfuscated PII to satisfy security review.
